weekly_recap.previous_weekend:
Carl Bruce squeaked past Daniel Bahamonde 100.92 to 94.74, a 6.18-point margin that will not sound dramatic until you hear this: it's the tightest game across the whole league this week, and every other blowout on the slate should feel embarrassed by comparison. This was also the third meeting between these two, and Carl now owns the series all-time, 3-0 — Daniel still hasn't found the door out of this particular basement.

Bijan Robinson torched the field for Daniel with 30.3 points, but DeVonta Smith no-showed for 1.3 and then closed out Monday Night Football still stuck at 1.3, officially sealing the loss in real time. Carl, meanwhile, got 29.8 points out of TreVeyon Henderson while Quentin Johnston contributed a goose egg — didn't matter.

Daniel — two-time last-place finisher who apparently spends his offseason getting photographed with Santa like that's a normal hobby for a grown man — adds another gut-punch to a career sitting under a 36% winning percentage. The loveable loser strikes again.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: Two guys sitting in the top six of the standings, and the "closest margin" billing still ended with Blake Pratt cruising 103.54 to 94.58, an 8.96-point gap that felt bigger once you realized Kevin Mallon's Chargers D/ST posted a nightmarish -1.0 points — the kind of number you get benched for even if you're a defense that technically can't be benched further. Derrick Henry bulldozed his way to 21.2 points for Pratt, who now leads their all-time series 1-0 after just one meeting. Mallon can log all the triathlon miles he wants — none of that cardio translates to reading a box score before it embarrasses him.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week:
Two teams stuck at 5-6, both mathematically alive and emotionally exhausted, but only one of these guys has to explain himself afterward — and it's Erik, who reportedly complains about every trade he makes, which is impressive given he's the one making them. His 2 Studs for a 6th squad is averaging 107.42 points a game this season, ranked 7th, clinging to a 40% playoff shot.

Across the way, triathlon-brained Kevin Mallon — presumably transitioning straight from a 20-minute morning jog into his lineup decisions — sits ranked 6th, averaging 113.82 points a game this season, and has somehow turned a tougher-than-average schedule into a 60% playoff outlook.

Kevin leads their all-time series 1-0, and with Erik's power score sitting at 19.5 against Kevin's 25.0, this smells like Erik's trade complaints are about to get a fresh, well-earned target.
